assumptions: Reuse the existing conservative bounded_initialization analyzer on the entire retained source closure before summary substitution, for both Crux forms.
A C++ cut without this source analysis stays unsupported, even if Crux could compile it.
An explicit shared source initializedness/origin-policy refusal ends the bounded chain; parse/read failures still follow the existing route.

The existing initialized-input restriction remains explicit: initialized scalars and distinct nonnull primitive harness buffers of exactly physical capacity. Logical sizes do not shorten those buffers.
changes: Direct Crux C/C++ refuses uninitialized locals and unsupported local/global aggregate origins, helper reads and pointer rebinding before bitcode or verifier launch.
Generator-owned replay rebuilds original closure, source admission, current summary stubs, harness and exact input bytes before execution and again at the final proof-setup boundary.
Records expose bounded_initialization and source_admission plus corresponding proof-setup hashes; source analyzer is pinned for both forms.
The fallback policy module is now a checked method dependency.
limitations: No real Crux/CBMC acceptance or refutation was run for this patch. Positive controls reach a fake reader that reports parse_error; they do not prove a source unit.
This is a conservative restricted-language admission, not a complete source-initializedness or C++ origin analysis. Broader C++ cuts, unsupported aggregate/storage/lifetime cases remain refused.
Explicit entry array domains and imported domain-bearing summary assumptions remain refused on Crux until separate checked source-operation/call alignment exists.

Generic imported-summary proof-source/bounds binding remains a separate known gap owned by the main session. Fresh stub identity alone does not certify summary eligibility; this patch leaves the delegated _summary selection unchanged.
The source-after-bitcode mutation controls are rejected by the existing generic input-hash gate; they are not evidence of a newly discovered public source-drift bypass.
red_green: Original public Crux C++ uninitialized discarded read reached the controlled reader and returned parse_error; now it is refused before bitcode and verifier.
Passing primitive source initially lacked initialization/source-admission proof-setup receipts; both receipts are now present on checked stand-in launches.
The bounded route initially attempted all three adapters after a source-policy refusal; now it stops at the first refusal.
Changing a copied bounded_chain.py initially left the frozen execution method usable; now method pinning rejects it before the scripted command.

review.scope: Independent read of Crux/bounded_chain/proof_setup diff confirmed both-form source admission, unchecked-cut refusal, fresh rebuild and policy termination; no human code review claimed.
